title: Capacity journey map: snapshot tiles, autoscale timeline, and SLA horizon visuals
creator: Ava Ramirez
description: Create a cohesive set of onboarding visuals that explain capacity setup, autoscaling behavior, and SLA trade-offs using a progressive disclosure approach. Deliverables: 1) a set of snapshot tiles (compact and expanded) that show capacity state, cost estimate, and recommended autoscale profile; 2) a horizontal autoscale timeline visualization with sample workloads and expected latency/cost curves; 3) an SLA horizon mini-chart that conveys P99/P95 targets vs observed distribution and fallback behavior; 4) tooltip copy and micro-illustrations for key knobs (burst, reserved pool, pre-warm); 5) annotated screenshots and an asset export for engineering (SVGs, 2x PNGs, CSS tokens). This ticket focuses on the visual language and handoff package; interaction specs (micro-animations) will be tracked in DES-35877. Aim for clarity for first-run users while enabling an "advanced" toggle for platform-savvy engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Snapshot tiles: compact and expanded variants created in Figma with tokenized spacing and color tokens; accessibility contrast pass
Autoscale timeline: clear lanes for reserved capacity, burst buffer, and predicted latency; data-driven example included
SLA horizon chart: communicates target bands and automatic fallback behavior when capacity is exhausted
Tooltip copy: final microcopy approved by PM and UX writer (<= 140 chars) for 6 controls
Handoff package: exported SVGs and 2x PNGs for 3 breakpoints, asset manifest, and a short README for engineers
Design review: PR in design critique completed and action items resolved
design_notes: Key decision: use snapshot tiles as the primary information radiators on first-run. Tiles should show immediate recommended action (e.g., 'Reserve N GPUs' or 'Enable burst') with an efficiency score. Autoscale timeline must avoid overloaded legends; use lane colors aligned with console palette and an optional raw-data toggle. For SLA horizon, use a shaded band approach rather than multiple lines to make variance readable to non-technical users. Prepare two A/B variants of microcopy: Simplified (for product-first audiences) and Technical (for infra/platform audiences).
tasks: Design autoscale timeline & create sample workload curves
Build SLA horizon visual and derive copy explaining fallback behavior
Run accessibility contrast and font-size checks
Export assets and write handoff README
